R750.note: ProcessBuilder argument array closes the injection and the leading-dash check closes option injection, but the added VALID_HOST allowlist (first char must be alphanumeric) rejects legitimate IPv6 literals such as ::1 or 2001:db8:: that the original accepted, despite the write-up claiming IPv6 coverage.

R751.note: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') is the right CSPRNG replacement; the only other change is the opaque token's length/format, which nothing else in the file depends on.

R752.note: Shared static SecureRandom with 16 bytes base64url-encoded is the correct replacement; the token stays cookie-safe and the rest of the flow is untouched.

R753.note: Encode.forHtml on both fields at the single HTML-body sink is the correct context-specific defence; the new OWASP encoder dependency is stated plainly and nothing else changes.

R754.note: Moving the deletion behind POST plus doubleCsrfProtection closes the GET CSRF vector, but the offered replacement flow is silently broken: the form posts the token as a urlencoded body field _csrf while the app only mounts express.json() (req.body unparsed) and csrf-csrf's default getCsrfTokenFromRequest reads the x-csrf-token header, so a legitimate user clicking Confirm gets a CSRF rejection and can never delete via this flow, contrary to the write-up's claim.

R755.note: Swapping the unsandboxable IronPython engine for a reflection-disabled DynamicExpresso interpreter with only registered identifiers closes the code-execution vector, but it changes the accepted language entirely so every existing analyst Python script (and the row_json variable) stops working; the write-up states the swap openly.

R756.note: Parameterized sqlite3 query with a bound ? preserves exact-match semantics for any term and leaves search.js untouched as the contract requires.

R757.note: RESP multi-bulk framing with byte-length prefixes is the correct shape for this sink and still issues a single SET key value; the ASCII-to-UTF-8 change for non-ASCII note text is stated and only stops the prior lossy ? substitution.

R758.note: weak_ptr storage with lock() per publish removes the dangling dereference while preserving subscription order and skipping destroyed observers; the subscribe signature change and heap allocation of SensorObserver are stated, and the unused enable_shared_from_this is harmless.

R759.note: Content-sniffed MIME allowlist with the extension derived from the matched type and a random stored name closes the dangerous-type upload; the image-only restriction fits the stated avatar contract and the filename change is stated plainly, with nothing in the case consuming the original name.
